rv.q: The heart of the show beats here with intensity.
Overall, the musical is close to perfection, filled with outstanding performances and heavenly gospel voices.
With Mack at the lead, this musical makes that range of emotions land.
Every second of this nearly three-hour show is wholeheartedly earned.
The Summer will be tinted violet by this gorgeous, regal presentation that’s quite simply, Too Beautiful for Words.
Brown doesn’t simply direct this musical; she honors it, restores it, and reminds us why this story still matters.
The Color Purple is onstage at the Goodman in a joyous, defiant, full-throated, and full-hearted revival, directed by Lili-Anne Brown.
Brown captures struggle and triumph with the fire of a preacher at a revival.
And their new production boasting Chicago superstar talent is this summer’s big prize!
Overall, Brown has masterfully developed an exceptional platform for this play, making it a Must-See production.
Simply put, Mack’s portrayal of Celie is one of the most soulful, finely tuned and convincing performances in recent memory.
The production's overall impact is diminished by its lack of subtlety.
But technical finesse can’t hide a fundamental hollowness.
This is a show not to be missed, a celebration of the human spirit that will leave you moved and inspired.
This is the level of quality theater you expect to see in a Chicago Loop production.
For those that may not have seen it before but have been waiting for the right production, this one is it.
“The Color Purple: The Musical” is a marvel, having won two Tony Awards in 2016 for best revival of a musical production.
